title: CBSE Declares Class 10 Second Board Exam Results With 96.78% Overall Pass Rate
excerpt: Nearly 60% of students who took the improvement exam scored higher than their first attempt, validating the NEP 2020 reform that introduced two board exams per year.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • CBSE's Class 10 second board exam results show a 96.78% overall pass rate.
  • 59.95% of students improved their scores in the improvement exam.
  • Compartment pass percentage increased to 52.40%, up from 48.68% last year.
  • The two-exam system under NEP 2020 allows students to keep their best score.

CBSE Results 2026
  • CBSE has declared Class 10 second board examination results for 2026, with an overall pass percentage of 96.78% after combining both exam attempts.
  • Of the 5.14 lakh students who took the improvement exam, 59.95% — roughly 3.08 lakh students — scored higher than their first attempt.
  • The compartment pass percentage rose to 52.40%, up from 48.68% in the previous year.
  • This is the first year the two-exam system operates under NEP 2020, allowing students to keep the better of their two scores.

A New Exam System Delivers Results

The Central Board of Secondary Education has declared the results of its Class 10 second board examination for 2026, marking the first full cycle of the two-exam-per-year system introduced under the National Education Policy 2020. The overall pass percentage, combining the main and second examinations, stands at 96.78%.

A total of 6,63,777 students appeared for the second exam, which was held between May 15 and May 21. Of these, 5,13,955 took the test specifically to improve their scores from the main examination held in February and March.

The results vindicate the reform's central premise: that a second chance can meaningfully lift outcomes. Of the students who sat for improvement, 3,08,095 — or 59.95% — achieved higher marks than their first attempt.

Compartment Students See Gains

For students in the compartment category — those who failed one or more subjects in the main exam — the second examination offered a crucial lifeline. A total of 1,49,822 compartment students appeared, and 78,503 passed, bringing the compartment pass percentage to 52.40%. That is a notable improvement over last year's 48.68%, suggesting the additional exam window is helping students who need it most.

How to Check Results

Results are available through multiple platforms. Students can access their scores at cbseresults.nic.in using their roll number, school number and admit card ID. Results are also available through the DigiLocker app and UMANG app. For students who prefer SMS, CBSE has set up a service: send "cbse10" followed by roll number, school code and centre number to 7738299899.

School-wise results are being shared with schools through their registered email addresses. Printed mark sheets and passing certificates for regular students will be distributed through their respective schools.

What NRI Families Need to Know

For the Indian diaspora, the two-exam reform has practical implications. Students studying in CBSE-affiliated schools abroad — found across the Gulf, Southeast Asia, Africa and beyond — can download their results and digital certificates through DigiLocker, eliminating the need for physical document collection. The digital academic documents are available through the CBSE repository.

The "better of two scores" policy means NRI students, like their counterparts in India, had the flexibility to attempt improvement without any downside risk. If the second score was lower, their original marks stood.

The Bigger Picture

The main board examination results, declared on April 15, had shown a 93.70% pass rate across 24.7 lakh students. The second exam has lifted the combined figure to 96.78%, demonstrating that the two-exam structure is delivering on its promise of reduced exam stress and improved outcomes. For the 3 lakh students who improved their scores, the difference could mean better options for Class 11 stream selection and, ultimately, college admissions.
